text.p: Opener Nick Knight restored some of England's battered pride with a century on the first day of the four-day match against Matabeleland at Bulawayo on Tuesday.
Knight spearheaded a much improved England batting performance which saw the tourists reach 199 for three at the end of a day reduced to 54 overs due to an afternoon rainstorm.

Alec Stewart and Nasser Hussain made 39 and 38 to gave Knight good support, but skipper Mike Atherton failed again at the top of the order when he had his middle stump knocked out by Zimbabwe opening bowler Henry Olonga.
Atherton's four runs gave him a total of just 13 from three first class innings on tour and his poor form is worrying ahead of the first one-day match against imbabwe at Bulawayo on Sunday.
Knight was the senior partner in a second wicket stand of 86 with Stewart and a third wicket stand of 85 with Hussain. The solid left hander brought up his ton in the last over of the day.
Knight, who scored a half century against the same opposition in Sunday's one-day match, reached his ton in four hours from 177 balls striking 14 fours.
